title: 2nd Mystery The Equality Of Few And Many Through The Mystery Of Luminosity And Obedience

questions.question: What is the main claim of the Second Mystery about Divine power and number?
questions.answer: It teaches that for Allah’s power, dealing with one thing and dealing with many things are equally easy.

questions.question: Which example shows how one source can appear in many places at once?
questions.answer: The example of the sun appearing in many reflective surfaces shows this.

questions.question: What three qualities are mentioned at the start to explain this ease of reflection and action?
questions.answer: Brightness, clearness, and readiness to follow the command are mentioned.

questions.question: In the mirror example, what is being emphasized more than the physical sun itself?
questions.answer: The point is that one source can give the same effect to countless receivers without becoming strained.

questions.question: How does the passage use the example of a spoken word?
questions.answer: It says one word can reach one listener and also many listeners with no extra difficulty in principle.

questions.question: What does the comparison between one ear and a million ears help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see that multiplying recipients does not limit boundless Divine activity.

questions.question: Which beings are used as examples of a single eye-like light or a luminous spirit?
questions.answer: A seeing light like an eye and a radiant spirit like Gabriel are used as examples.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can such a luminous being do through Divine power?
questions.answer: It can be present in, look into, or enter many places as easily as one place.

questions.question: What idea is repeated by saying there is no difference between great and small, and between many and few?
questions.answer: The repeated idea is that Divine power is not hindered by size or number.

questions.question: What role does Divine command play in this passage?
questions.answer: Divine command is presented as the basis by which this wide-reaching action takes place.

questions.question: What can be inferred about limits from the phrase about unrestricted power and boundless creativity?
questions.answer: It implies that created limits do not apply to Allah’s power and creativity.

questions.question: What central truth is the Second Mystery trying to make understandable?
questions.answer: It is explaining why multiplicity does not make things harder for Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage begin with images of light and reflection?
questions.answer: Those images help the mind picture how one reality can be connected to many places at once.

questions.question: In the example of the sun and mirrors, what remains the same whether the mirrors are few or many?
questions.answer: The sun’s ability to give its reflection remains the same.

questions.question: Besides reflected brightness, what other effects are said to be given as well?
questions.answer: Warmth is also included along with light.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the statement that large and small are alike?
questions.answer: The lesson is that scale does not create difficulty for Divine power.

questions.question: How is hearing used as a second comparison?
questions.answer: The passage compares one statement reaching one person with that same statement reaching many people.

questions.question: What does the phrase about dominical permission add to the example of the spoken word?
questions.answer: It shows that this wide reach happens by Allah’s leave and rule, not independently.

questions.question: Why is Gabriel mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Gabriel is mentioned as an example of a luminous being whose presence in many places can be understood through Divine power.

questions.question: What three actions are mentioned regarding presence in multiple places?
questions.answer: Being present, looking, and entering are the three actions.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is the passage using overall: purely physical science, moral advice, or analogy for faith?
questions.answer: It is using analogy for faith.

questions.question: What misunderstanding is the passage trying to remove from the reader’s mind?
questions.answer: It is removing the assumption that more beings automatically means more difficulty for Allah.

questions.question: In one sentence, summarize the full teaching of the passage.
questions.answer: Because Allah’s power is unrestricted and His command effective, reaching one or reaching countless beings makes no difference to Him.

questions.question: According to the Second Mystery, what does the example of the sun teach about a single source and many recipients?
questions.answer: It teaches that one source can give the same manifestation to countless recipients at once.

questions.question: Why are mirrors, shiny surfaces, and drops all mentioned together?
questions.answer: They show different kinds and numbers of receiving places, yet all can receive the same reflection.

questions.question: What point is made by saying the same gift reaches both the big and the small?
questions.answer: The point is that difference in size does not affect the ease of Divine action.

questions.question: How does the human example of speech support the same message?
questions.answer: A single utterance can be heard by many people without becoming divided or weakened in the way the passage wants to illustrate.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by describing creativity as boundless?
questions.answer: It means Allah’s creative action is not confined by human-style limits.

questions.question: What is the significance of using both physical examples and spiritual examples in the same passage?
questions.answer: It shows that the principle applies across different levels of existence, not only in material things.

questions.question: How does the example of an eye function in the passage?
questions.answer: It serves as an image of a light-giving presence that can direct attention without being trapped in one narrow spot.

questions.question: What does the mention of a radiant spirit suggest about the nature of non-material beings?
questions.answer: It suggests they can act in ways not limited like dense physical bodies, by Allah’s power.

questions.question: What repeated contrast structures the whole paragraph?
questions.answer: The repeated contrast is one versus many, and small versus great.

questions.question: Is the passage mainly stressing effort, method, or authority? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: It is mainly stressing authority, because the action happens through Divine command and power.

questions.question: How would this passage answer someone who thinks managing many things must be harder than managing one?
questions.answer: It would answer that such difficulty belongs to created beings, not to Allah, whose power reaches many as easily as one.

questions.question: What is the core message repeated at the beginning and end of the target passage?
questions.answer: The message is that plurality does not create difficulty for Divine power.

questions.question: In the first comparison, what allows one sun to be seen in many reflecting surfaces?
questions.answer: Its light can appear in many receivers at the same time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of mentioning not just mirrors but also bright objects and drops of water?
questions.answer: The purpose is to widen the example and show that many kinds of receivers can display the same manifestation.

questions.question: According to the passage, does the number of receiving places reduce the source’s ability to act?
questions.answer: No, the source’s action is presented as equally easy regardless of number.

questions.question: What everyday experience is used to make the teaching easier to grasp?
questions.answer: Hearing one statement with many ears is used as an everyday example.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the vastness of creative activity suggest about Allah’s acts?
questions.answer: It suggests His acts are not cramped, local, or restricted.

questions.question: How does the example of Gabriel deepen the discussion beyond physical light?
questions.answer: It moves from material illustration to a spiritual example, showing that Divine power is not limited to physical processes.

questions.question: What does the passage say a luminous being can do in many places?
questions.answer: It can be present, observe, or enter many places with equal ease.

questions.question: What kind of equality is being claimed when the passage says there is no difference between many and few?
questions.answer: It is claiming equality in ease from the perspective of Divine power.

questions.question: What false assumption about power does this passage challenge?
questions.answer: It challenges the idea that power must become strained when its objects increase.

questions.question: Give a brief interpretive summary of the whole passage.
questions.answer: The passage argues by analogy that Allah’s command and power are so expansive that one and many, or small and great, stand on the same level before Him.

questions.question: What does the title “Second Mystery” introduce in this passage?
questions.answer: It introduces a further explanation of how Allah can act upon countless things with the same ease as upon one thing.

questions.question: Which natural image opens the explanation?
questions.answer: The opening image is the sun giving its appearance to many reflectors.

questions.question: What does this image teach about multiplication of effects?
questions.answer: It teaches that one cause can produce many corresponding appearances without difficulty.

questions.question: What are readers meant to notice about the phrase comparing big and small?
questions.answer: They are meant to notice that difference in size does not matter for Allah’s power.

questions.question: How does the example of one statement reaching many ears build on the first example?
questions.answer: It shifts from sight to hearing while keeping the same lesson that many recipients do not create extra burden.

questions.question: What does the passage connect to this wide reach besides power itself?
questions.answer: It connects it to Divine command and the vast range of creative activity.

questions.question: Why might the passage choose an angelic example after examples from daily life?
questions.answer: It helps the reader move from familiar experiences to a broader understanding of unseen realities.

questions.question: In the example of a luminous spirit, what is said to be equally easy?
questions.answer: Being in one place and being in many places are presented as equally easy through Divine power.

questions.question: What theological conclusion should the reader draw from these examples?
questions.answer: The reader should conclude that Allah’s power is not measured by created standards of effort, division, or limitation.

questions.question: How does this passage strengthen trust in Allah’s complete ability?
questions.answer: It trains the mind to see that nothing becomes unmanageable for Him just because it is numerous, widespread, or large.

questions.question: What problem in human thinking is the Second Mystery correcting?
questions.answer: It is correcting the habit of imagining Allah’s power as if it worked like limited human power.

questions.question: Why is light a fitting starting point for the argument?
questions.answer: Light helps show how one thing can reach many places at once in a way people can picture.

questions.question: What does the sun example say about giving the same effect to countless receivers?
questions.answer: It says this can happen with ease, without any real distinction between few and many.

questions.question: In that first example, what kinds of receivers are named?
questions.answer: Mirrors, bright surfaces, and drops are named.

questions.question: How does the passage move from visible examples to less visible realities?
questions.answer: It starts with sunlight, then speech, then a spiritual being.

questions.question: What is the point of the example about one word and many ears?
questions.answer: The point is that one act can extend to many hearers without becoming difficult in the way we usually assume.

questions.question: What does “with dominical permission” teach about how such things occur?
questions.answer: It teaches that these effects happen under Allah’s authority and allowance.

questions.question: What is special about the example involving Gabriel?
questions.answer: It shows that even a single spiritual being may relate to many places through Allah’s power.

questions.question: Which actions toward many places are specifically mentioned?
questions.answer: Presence, seeing, and entering are specifically mentioned.

questions.question: What repeated statement gives the passage its conclusion?
questions.answer: The conclusion is that there is no meaningful difference between greater and smaller, or more and fewer, for Divine power.

questions.question: What style of teaching is being used here to help belief?
questions.answer: The passage uses layered analogies to guide the reader from simple examples to a theological conclusion.

questions.question: If you had to state the passage’s message in a faith-centered way for a Muslim college student, what would you say?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is not boxed in by size, distance, or numbers, so what seems overwhelming to us is equally easy for Him.
